packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

PACKET-05 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
this item or an earlier reading. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files of
this packet (packet.json not read). No web or search tool used.

== LAYOUT SURVEY (from image-001.jpg, reduced overview with ruler) ==

Observations:
- One face of a small, irregular fragment, about 14.5 cm wide and about 9.5 cm
  high by the ruler. Landscape as photographed; the writing runs horizontally
  and upright, so the orientation is correct for reading.
- Support looks like laid paper (close horizontal laid lines visible in the
  clean areas at upper right and upper centre), heavily stained brown, with
  paste or surface residue over much of the left half and a band across the
  right half. Upper edge torn away in a deep bite at centre; left and lower left
  edges torn; right and bottom edges look cut straight. Two small holes.
- A vertical fold or crease about 4.5 cm from the left edge divides the face
  into a narrow left strip and a wide right block. The left strip carries the
  line-ends of a block of text (its beginnings are lost to the left); the right
  block carries line-beginnings that start just right of the crease.
  Tentative interpretation: two columns, or the two pages of an opening of a
  small bifolium, with the crease as the gutter. I cannot tell which.
- Script: a rapid grey-brown cursive, single hand as far as visible. About 14
  to 15 lines survive in the right block, the upper ones only in part.
- No running title, rubric, coloured initial, underlining, or interlinear gloss
  is visible. The line beginning near the bottom of the right block (about the
  fourth line from the end) starts with a somewhat larger letter at the left
  margin after a short preceding line, which may mark a new paragraph
  (tentative).
- Faint show-through of writing from the other side is visible at the top
  right, upside down or mirrored relative to the main text.

== GROUP 1: image-002.jpg (upper left tile) and image-003.jpg (upper right tile) ==

The two tiles overlap horizontally: the right edge of image-002 repeats the
left edge of image-003 (the area around the small hole with a brown fleck).
Lines R2 to R8 below are each ONE physical line seen across both tiles, not two
lines. Line numbers are counted from the top of each image and are approximate
because the top lines are fragmentary.

General condition of this group: the ink is a pale grey wash, abraded and
partly under residue. Letter shapes are visible but few words are secure. Most
of what follows is letter-level reading with heavy uncertainty; I have marked
it so and have not completed words from sense.

--- Left strip (line-ENDS only; beginnings lost at the torn left edge) ---
image-002 L1 (top left corner):  [illegible] ...mo? [traces only]
image-002 L2:  ...mi[illegible]s? [then residue]
image-002 L3:  [illegible - under brown residue]

--- Right block (line-BEGINNINGS start just right of the crease) ---

Notes: the top right of image-003 shows horizontal laid lines and faint

== GROUP 2: image-004.jpg (lower left tile) and image-005.jpg (lower right tile) ==

These overlap each other horizontally, and their top lines overlap the bottom
lines of image-002 and image-003 (left-strip "...o volūt" and right-block R9,
R10 are the same lines seen again). The ink is a little firmer here; this is
the most legible part of the face, but still mostly uncertain.

--- Left strip (line-ENDS only), image-004 ---

               or point (line appears to end short)

image-004 L8 (lowest, by the crease):  ...[illegible]ny? / ...ous?
Below L7 the left strip is torn away diagonally.

    dema(n)da[..]la? [residue] ...i(n)dagac(i)o(n)em? / gradac(i)o(n)em? p(ro)?
    fid(e)s? / fid(e)i? li[illegible]
R11 image-004 L3 / image-005 L4:
    Su(m)ma(m)? / Enumā(n)d(um)? d(e)? is[illegible] ... [brown blot] ...
    p(ri)ma? ad? / ad(huc)?   [line appears to stop about mid-width; rest
    blank or lost]
R12 image-004 L4 / image-005 L4-5:
    ī cast[..]te? / ī castro? [illegible]n? sp(irit)u? . [illegible]
    [the right half of this line is not legible to me]
R13 image-004 L5 / image-005 L6:   (begins with a larger letter at the margin;
    possible paragraph opening - tentative)
    Qui? / Qm̄? d(icitu)r? [abraded gap] ...mi[..]? nat(ur)a? / natus? D(omi)ni? /
    Divini? mens? / n(ost)ri? Sig(n)i? / Dign(e)? d(icitu)r? p[illegible]
R14 image-004 L6 / image-005 L7:
    īvolutū? / moleti? (et) c(etera)? / (et) ca[..]? Nota? / hoc? q(uod)? /
    Q(uia)? lat(us) p(er)foratū [..]o? s[illegible]
      - "lat(us) p(er)foratū" is the reading on this face I am most confident
        of: l-a-t with a 9-shaped -us sign, then crossed p (per) + "foratu"
        with a bar. The words before it are less sure.
R15 image-004 L7 / image-005 L8:
    sangui(n)e? / sanguis? [C/O][..]n[..]m? s[..]ssi(m)e? / sc(ri)ssu(m)?
    man(us)? / mar(ie)? [paper surface lost] ...p(ro)[..]mine? / tp[..]mine? a
    ch[..]? / d[..]?
      - "sangui..." at the line opening is fairly clear (long s, a, n, g, u/i
        minims with a mark above); its ending is not.
R16 image-004 L8 / image-005 L9 (last line, partly cut by the lower edge):
    [p with stroke] p(ri)mū? / ip(s)i(us)? o[..]? [..]tm̄? / cu(m)? vim? / una?
    miss[..]? / inisi[..]? [surface lost] ... [further right, slightly higher,
    possibly the end of R15 or of this line:] ...ens? / ...eus? d(icitu)r? / ð

The lower right corner of image-005 below R16 is blank paper to the cut edge.

== SELECTION, UNREAD AREAS, LIMITATIONS ==

- Selected: all visible lines, since the face is small. There is no heading,
  rubric or question opening to anchor on; the only structural feature is the
  possible paragraph opening at R13.
- Effectively unread: the whole left strip (line-ends only, and under residue);
  R1 to R8 of the right block beyond isolated letter groups; the right-hand
  ends of R11, R12 and R16.
- Words I would treat as usable for a later match, in descending confidence:
  "lat(us) p(er)foratū" (R14); "sangui..." (R15 opening); "volūt" (left strip);
  "se quas(i)?" (left strip); "in fide?" (R9); "p(ri)ma" (R7, R11). Everything
  else is a letter-shape guess and should not be used as evidence.
- Language: the abbreviation system and the few secure words are Latin. Some
  letter groups in R2 and R5-R6 did not resolve as Latin for me; I cannot say
  whether that is another language or simply my failure to read abraded Latin.
- I did not supply any word from sense or from memory of any text. Several
  alternatives are given precisely because I could not decide between them.
- Line counts are approximate: the upper edge is torn and R1 is only letter
  feet, so absolute line numbers of the original page are unknown.
- Column question unresolved: left strip and right block may be two columns of
  one page or two pages of a folded sheet. Line spacing looks similar on both
  sides of the crease but the lines do not obviously align.
- A wider view would not help (the overview already shows the whole face).
  What would help: a raking-light or infrared/UV image of this face, and the
  other face of the fragment (show-through at upper right indicates writing
  there).

This is an unverified image reading.
